docs.title: Cortex MCP Server Overview
docs.text:
Cortex is a local-first AI second-brain: a system for capturing fleeting notes ("thoughts"), maintaining a structured knowledge wiki, and making everything semantically searchable — all from within an AI assistant conversation via MCP tools.

The server is designed so that nothing leaves your machine. Embeddings are generated by a local Ollama instance, persistence lives in a local Supabase Postgres database with pgvector, and the wiki is a directory of plain markdown files on your filesystem.

docs.title: What Cortex Does
docs.text:
Cortex manages two complementary knowledge stores:

Thoughts are atomic, self-contained notes — observations, decisions, ideas, tasks, person notes, or references. When a thought is captured, Cortex automatically generates a vector embedding and calls a local LLM to extract structured metadata: the note type, topic tags, people mentioned, and any action items. Thoughts are stored in a Supabase entries table and are immediately searchable by semantic similarity.

WikiVault is a curated, LLM-maintained knowledge base of structured pages — people, projects, concepts, areas, topics, and imported raw materials (articles, books, daily notes). Pages are markdown files with YAML frontmatter stored in a configurable directory (default ~/Documents/Obsidian/WikiVault/). Each page is also indexed into the same entries table so thoughts and wiki content can be searched together or independently. An index.md is rebuilt automatically, and every significant write is appended to log.md as an audit trail.

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
All searchable content shares a single entries table in Supabase Postgres:

Column Purpose content Raw text of the thought or wiki page body embedding 4096-dimensional vector from qwen3-embedding via Ollama source Origin: web, discord, mcp, api, or wiki metadata JSONB: type, topics, people, action_items file_path, title, page_type Wiki-only: filesystem location and page classification tags, wikilinks, page_sources, cortex_ids Wiki-only: relational context

Deduplication is handled by a upsert_entry Postgres RPC that computes a SHA-256 fingerprint over normalized content. Semantic search uses a match_entries RPC with pgvector cosine similarity. Chat messages are stored in a separate messages table, also embedded and searchable.

docs.title: Thought Capture and Retrieval
docs.text:
capture_thought is the primary ingestion tool. It takes a single string and handles embedding, metadata extraction, and deduplication automatically. Retrieval is served by three tools that cover different query patterns:

  • search_thoughts — semantic similarity search over thoughts only
  • list_thoughts — chronological browse with filters for type, topic, person, and recency
  • thought_stats — aggregate overview: total count, type breakdown, top topics and people

docs.title: Wiki Management
docs.text:
The wiki tools follow a read-before-write discipline. read_wiki_page retrieves a page by title or file path (pure filesystem, no database). write_wiki_page creates or overwrites a page — it merges frontmatter, auto-extracts [[wikilinks]], re-embeds, and re-indexes. append_wiki_log appends an audit entry to log.md and should be called after every significant wiki action.

Browsing is handled by: - search_wiki — semantic search restricted to wiki pages, with optional page-type filter - list_wiki_pages — filesystem scan returning title, type, tags, and path; no database required

docs.title: Cross-Corpus Search
docs.text:
search_all queries the unified entries table without a source filter, returning both thoughts and wiki pages ranked by relevance. Results are labelled [thought] or [wiki:type]. It uses a lower default similarity threshold (0.45) for broader recall and is the right choice when you want the fullest possible context.

search_messages searches the separate chat history (messages table), covering everything discussed in past AI conversation sessions.

docs.title: Vault Migration
docs.text: migrate_vault_file is a one-time import tool for bringing files from a MainVault (e.g. an existing Obsidian vault) into WikiVault's raw/ subtree. It strips Dataview blocks, adds standardized frontmatter, embeds, and indexes — without modifying the source file.

docs.title: MCP Transport
docs.text:
Cortex supports two transports, both backed by the same createCortexServer() factory in src/server/routes/mcp.ts:

Transport Entry point When to use stdio src/server/mcp-stdio.ts Claude Desktop — spawned as a subprocess Streamable HTTP POST /mcp on port 3001 Cursor, custom agents, any HTTP MCP client

The HTTP endpoint accepts an optional x-cortex-key header or ?key= query parameter for authentication. If MCP_ACCESS_KEY is not set in the environment, authentication is skipped entirely.

docs.title: Companion Interfaces
docs.text:
The same Node.js/Express process that hosts the MCP endpoint also serves:

  • REST API — /api/thoughts, /api/wiki, /api/chat, /api/conversations — used by the web UI and available for direct HTTP clients
  • React web UI — Vite + React 19 frontend on port 5173 with Capture, Browse, Search, and Stats tabs
  • Discord bot — optional; auto-captures messages in a configured channel and responds to !search, !recent, !ask, and !stats commands

All three share the same core library functions in src/server/lib/ — particularly captureThought() in capture.ts and the wiki operations in wiki.ts — so behavior is consistent regardless of which interface is used.

docs.title: Multi-Step Usage Workflows
docs.text:
Capturing and synthesizing knowledge

  1. Call capture_thought as insights arise throughout a session — each is embedded and tagged automatically.
  2. Later, call search_thoughts or search_all to retrieve relevant prior context on a topic.
  3. Call search_wiki or read_wiki_page to check whether a structured page already exists.
  4. Call read_wiki_page to read the existing page before modifying it.
  5. Call write_wiki_page to create or update the wiki page, synthesizing newly captured thoughts.
  6. Call append_wiki_log to record what was done.

Answering a question with full context

  1. Call search_all with a broad query to get the widest possible picture.
  2. Follow up with search_messages to surface anything discussed in prior chat sessions.
  3. Use list_thoughts with a person or topic filter for targeted retrieval.
  4. Call read_wiki_page on any directly relevant wiki entries.

Onboarding existing notes

  1. Call migrate_vault_file for each MainVault file, specifying the appropriate target_type.
  2. Call search_wiki to verify the imported content is indexed and searchable.
  3. Create or update wiki summary pages with write_wiki_page, linking to the raw imports via page_sources.

Process entry points:

  • src/server/app.ts — constructs the Express app and wires all route modules; exported separately for testability.
  • src/server/mcp-stdio.ts — standalone entry point that calls createCortexServer() and connects via StdioServerTransport. Claude Desktop spawns this as a subprocess.

docs.title: Persistence Layer
docs.text:
All captured content — thoughts and wiki pages — shares a single entries table in Supabase Postgres. The schema is defined in supabase/migrations/004_entries.sql.

entries table key columns:

Column Type Purpose id uuid Primary key content text Original content embedding vector(4096) Semantic embedding source text web, discord, mcp, api, or wiki metadata jsonb Type, topics, people, action items (thoughts) file_path text Relative path in WikiVault (wiki pages) title text Human-readable title (wiki pages) page_type text Wiki page type (wiki pages) tags text[] Topic tags (wiki pages) wikilinks text[] Extracted [[wikilink]] refs (wiki pages) fingerprint text SHA-256 of normalized content

Deduplication is handled server-side by the upsert_entry RPC: if a row with the same SHA-256 fingerprint already exists, the RPC returns the existing row with duplicate: true rather than inserting a duplicate.

Semantic search is handled by the match_entries RPC, which applies pgvector cosine similarity. The source_filter argument lets callers restrict results to thoughts only (['web','discord','mcp','api']), wiki only (['wiki']), or across all entries (null).

Chat history lives in a separate messages table (joined to a conversations table), populated by the SSE chat endpoint in routes/chat.ts and searchable via a dedicated search_messages RPC.

docs.title: Inference Stack
docs.text:
All inference runs locally through Ollama. Model names are configured in src/server/lib/config.ts and are overridable via environment variables.

Role Default model Env var Embeddings qwen3-embedding (4096-d) EMBEDDING_MODEL Chat glm-4.7-flash CHAT_MODEL Metadata extraction glm-5:cloud METADATA_MODEL

Embedding flow for a captured thought:

  1. captureThought() in src/server/lib/capture.ts calls Ollama to embed the content and extractMetadata() in parallel.
  2. extractMetadata() in src/server/lib/metadata.ts calls Ollama chat with a structured prompt; response parsing handles raw JSON, fenced code blocks, text-wrapped JSON, and <think> blocks, with a safe default on any failure.
  3. upsert_entry RPC writes (or skips) the row.

The same captureThought() function is called by the HTTP REST route, the Discord bot, and the capture_thought MCP tool — there is no separate ingestion path.

docs.title: WikiVault Filesystem
docs.text:
The WikiVault is a directory tree of markdown files at the path configured by WIKI_VAULT_PATH (default ~/Documents/Obsidian/WikiVault/). All file I/O is handled by src/server/lib/wiki.ts using gray-matter for YAML frontmatter.

Directory structure:

WikiVault/
├── wiki/
│   ├── people/
│   ├── projects/
│   ├── concepts/
│   ├── areas/
│   └── topics/
├── raw/
│   ├── articles/
│   ├── books/
│   ├── daily/
│   └── attachments/
├── SCHEMA.md
├── index.md   ← auto-rebuilt by write_wiki_page on new pages
└── log.md     ← append-only audit trail

Every write_wiki_page call: 1. Merges with any existing frontmatter (preserves created, bumps updated). 2. Auto-extracts wikilinks[] from [[ref]] patterns in the body. 3. Writes the file via gray-matter. 4. Re-reads the file and calls upsert_entry with source='wiki' so the page participates in all semantic searches alongside thoughts. 5. Appends a log line to log.md and rebuilds index.md for new pages.

Wiki pages are never stored only in the filesystem — the Supabase entries table always holds a synchronized, embedded copy.

docs.title: MCP Layer
docs.text:
All 12 MCP tools are registered in a single factory function createCortexServer() in src/server/routes/mcp.ts. This factory is consumed in two places:

  • routes/mcp.ts mounts it behind the POST /mcp Streamable HTTP endpoint, with optional x-cortex-key / ?key= authentication controlled by the MCP_ACCESS_KEY env var.
  • mcp-stdio.ts calls the same factory and connects it via StdioServerTransport for Claude Desktop.

Because both transports share one factory, adding a tool in createCortexServer() automatically exposes it to all MCP clients with no additional wiring.

Tool handlers call into the same lib/ helpers used by REST routes and the Discord bot:

MCP tool handler
  └─▶  lib/capture.ts  captureThought()
  └─▶  lib/wiki.ts     readWikiPage() / writeWikiPage()
  └─▶  lib/ollama.ts   ollama.embed() / ollama.chat()
  └─▶  lib/supabase.ts supabase.rpc('match_entries', …)

docs.title: Extension Guide
docs.text: Cortex is designed to grow. All ingestion paths (HTTP, MCP, Discord) share the same library functions, and all MCP clients (Claude Desktop via stdio, Cursor via HTTP) are served by the same tool factory. Adding a new capability in one place exposes it everywhere.

docs.title: Adding a New MCP Tool
docs.text: All MCP tools are registered inside the createCortexServer() factory function in src/server/routes/mcp.ts. Both the HTTP /mcp endpoint and the stdio entry point (src/server/mcp-stdio.ts) call this same factory, so one registration covers all clients.

docs.title: Registration pattern
docs.text:
// src/server/routes/mcp.ts  (inside createCortexServer())

server.registerTool(
  "my_new_tool",
  {
    title: "My New Tool",
    description: "What this tool does and when an agent should call it.",
    inputSchema: z.object({
      required_param: z.string().describe("What this param is"),
      optional_param: z.number().default(10).describe("How many results (default 10)"),
    }),
  },
  async ({ required_param, optional_param }) => {
    try {
      const result = await myLibraryFunction(required_param, optional_param);
      return {
        content: [{ type: "text", text: result }],
      };
    } catch (err) {
      return {
        content: [{ type: "text", text: `Error: ${String(err)}` }],
        isError: true,
      };
    }
  }
);

docs.title: Handler return contract
docs.text:
Field Type Required Notes content Array<{ type: 'text', text: string }> Yes At least one element isError boolean No Set true when the handler catches an error instead of throwing

Always catch errors inside the handler and return isError: true rather than throwing — uncaught exceptions crash the MCP request cycle.

docs.title: Input schema tips
docs.text:
• Use zod objects for all input schemas. The SDK validates incoming calls against the schema before invoking the handler.
  • Add .describe("...") to every field — descriptions appear in the tool manifest that AI agents read.
  • Use .default(value) for optional parameters so handlers receive a usable value even when the client omits the field.

docs.title: Sharing Logic Between MCP Tools and REST Routes
docs.text:
Business logic belongs in src/server/lib/, not in route files. Both MCP handlers and REST routes import from lib.

Existing examples: - src/server/lib/capture.ts — captureThought() is called by POST /api/thoughts, the Discord bot (lib/discord.ts), and the capture_thought MCP tool. - src/server/lib/wiki.ts — readWikiPage(), writeWikiPage(), listWikiPages() are called by both routes/wiki.ts (REST) and multiple MCP tool handlers.

docs.title: Adding a new lib helper
docs.text:
1. Create src/server/lib/my-feature.ts and export pure functions.
  2. Import from both the MCP tool handler in routes/mcp.ts and from a new or existing REST route.
  3. Add a test file at tests/server/my-feature.test.ts (see Testing conventions).

docs.title: Adding a new REST route
docs.text:
1. Create src/server/routes/my-feature.ts exporting an Express Router.
  2. Mount it in src/server/app.ts: 
    import myFeatureRoutes from "./routes/my-feature.js";
app.use("/api", myFeatureRoutes);

docs.title: Adding a New Entry Source
docs.text:
Every captured entry has a source string stored verbatim in entries.source. Current values: web, discord, mcp, api, wiki.

To add a new source (e.g. slack):

  1. Capture: call captureThought(content, 'slack') from wherever you ingest the new data.

  2. Decide exclusion behavior: thought-only queries filter with source != 'wiki'. If your new source should also be excluded from thought-only results, update the exclusion filter in three places:

  3. src/server/routes/thoughts.ts — REST thought endpoints
  4. src/server/lib/discord.ts — Discord bot search

  5. src/server/routes/mcp.ts — the search_thoughts and list_thoughts tool handlers

  6. search_all is automatic: search_all uses source_filter: null (no filter) and will include the new source automatically with no changes needed.

// Example: a new Slack ingestor
import { captureThought } from "../lib/capture.js";

async function handleSlackMessage(text: string) {
  const result = await captureThought(text, "slack");
  console.log(`Captured ${result.duplicate ? "(duplicate)" : "new"} thought: ${result.id}`);
}

docs.title: Adding a New Wiki Page Type
docs.text: Wiki page types determine which subfolder a page is written to and which values appear in page_type frontmatter. The canonical list lives in src/server/lib/wiki.ts.

docs.title: Step-by-step
docs.text:
1. src/server/lib/wiki.ts — add to the WikiPageType union and WIKI_PAGE_TYPES array, and add a TYPE_DIR mapping entry: 

    export type WikiPageType =
  | "wiki_person"
  | "wiki_project"
  // ... existing types ...
  | "wiki_glossary";          // ← add here

export const WIKI_PAGE_TYPES: WikiPageType[] = [
  // ... existing entries ...
  "wiki_glossary",            // ← add here
];

const TYPE_DIR: Record<WikiPageType, string> = {
  // ... existing mappings ...
  wiki_glossary: "wiki/glossary",   // ← new subfolder
};

  2. src/server/routes/mcp.ts — update the zod enum in four tool definitions:

Tool Parameter write_wiki_page type search_wiki type list_wiki_pages type migrate_vault_file target_type (only if the new type is a raw_* variant) 
// Example: write_wiki_page type enum
type: z.enum([
  "wiki_person",
  "wiki_project",
  "wiki_concept",
  "wiki_area",
  "wiki_topic",
  "wiki_glossary",      // ← add here
  "raw_article",
  "raw_book",
  "raw_daily",
  "raw_attachment",
]).describe("Page type — determines which subfolder"),

  1. Database: if your Supabase schema enforces a page_type check constraint, update it in a new SQL migration file under supabase/migrations/.

  2. Filesystem: create the new subfolder under WIKI_VAULT_PATH before writing the first page of that type.

docs.title: Testing Conventions
docs.text:
Tests live in tests/server/ and run with vitest. Ollama and Supabase clients are mocked — tests do not require running services.

Reference file: tests/server/capture.test.ts — the canonical pattern for testing lib helpers.

docs.title: Adding a test for a new lib helper
docs.text:
// tests/server/my-feature.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from "vitest";

// Mock external dependencies before importing the module under test
vi.mock("../../src/server/lib/ollama", () => ({
  ollama: { embed: vi.fn() },
}));
vi.mock("../../src/server/lib/supabase", () => ({
  supabase: { rpc: vi.fn() },
}));

import { myLibraryFunction } from "../../src/server/lib/my-feature.js";
import { ollama } from "../../src/server/lib/ollama.js";
import { supabase } from "../../src/server/lib/supabase.js";

describe("myLibraryFunction", () => {
  beforeEach(() => vi.clearAllMocks());

  it("returns expected output for valid input", async () => {
    (ollama.embed as vi.Mock).mockResolvedValue({ embeddings: [[0.1, 0.2]] });
    (supabase.rpc as vi.Mock).mockResolvedValue({ data: [{ id: "abc" }], error: null });

    const result = await myLibraryFunction("test input");
    expect(result).toBeDefined();
  });

  it("handles Supabase errors gracefully", async () => {
    (supabase.rpc as vi.Mock).mockResolvedValue({ data: null, error: { message: "DB error" } });
    await expect(myLibraryFunction("test input")).rejects.toThrow("DB error");
  });
});

Run the full suite:

npm test

Run a single file during development:

npx vitest run tests/server/my-feature.test.ts

docs.title: Setup Guide
docs.text: Cortex requires four external services to be running before the server starts: Ollama (local LLM inference), Supabase (Postgres + pgvector, running in Docker), a WikiVault directory on the filesystem, and optionally a Discord bot token. Follow the steps in order.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
Requirement Version / Notes Node.js LTS recommended; install via nvm npm Bundled with Node.js Docker + Docker Compose Required for local Supabase Supabase CLI npm install -g supabase Ollama ollama.ai — must be running locally Git To clone the repo

Clone the repository and install dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/your-org/cortex.git
cd cortex
npm install

docs.title: 2. Start Ollama and Pull Models
docs.text:
Cortex needs three Ollama models. The embedding model is mandatory; the others default to the values below but can be overridden via env vars.

# Start the Ollama daemon (runs on http://localhost:11434 by default)
ollama serve

# Required: 4096-dimensional embedding model
ollama pull qwen3-embedding

# Required: chat/assistant model
ollama pull glm-4.7-flash

# Optional: cloud-routed metadata extraction model
ollama pull glm-5:cloud

If Ollama is on a different host or port, set OLLAMA_HOST in your .env (step 4).

docs.title: 3. Start Local Supabase and Apply Migrations
docs.text:
# Start Supabase in Docker (first run downloads images — allow a few minutes)
supabase start

Supabase surfaces a Studio dashboard at http://localhost:8000. The CLI prints the local API URL and service_role key — you will need both for your .env.

docs.title: Apply migrations
docs.text:
Open the Supabase SQL editor (Studio → SQL Editor) and run the migration files in order:

supabase/migrations/001_*.sql   # conversations + messages tables
supabase/migrations/002_*.sql
supabase/migrations/003_*.sql
supabase/migrations/004_entries.sql   # ← most important

004_entries.sql creates:

  • entries table — unified store for thoughts and wiki pages, with a vector(4096) embedding column, JSONB metadata, and wiki-specific columns (file_path, title, page_type, tags, wikilinks, page_sources, cortex_ids).
  • upsert_entry RPC — SHA-256 content fingerprint deduplication; returns duplicate: true if the content already exists.
  • match_entries RPC — pgvector cosine similarity search with optional source and JSONB filters.

The messages table (for chat history) and match_messages RPC are created by the earlier migration files.

docs.text:
Copy the example file and fill in each value:

cp .env.example .env

docs.title: 5. Create the WikiVault Directory Structure
docs.text:
The WikiVault is a plain directory of markdown files. Create it manually before starting the server:

WIKI_VAULT_PATH="${WIKI_VAULT_PATH:-$HOME/Documents/Obsidian/WikiVault}"

mkdir -p "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/wiki/people"
mkdir -p "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/wiki/projects"
mkdir -p "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/wiki/concepts"
mkdir -p "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/wiki/areas"
mkdir -p "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/wiki/topics"
mkdir -p "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/raw/articles"
mkdir -p "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/raw/books"
mkdir -p "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/raw/daily"
mkdir -p "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/raw/attachments"

# Create required stub files
touch "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/SCHEMA.md"
touch "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/index.md"
touch "$WIKI_VAULT_PATH/log.md"

index.md is rebuilt automatically by write_wiki_page. log.md is appended by append_wiki_log and tracks every significant wiki action. SCHEMA.md is reserved for documentation of your vault's conventions — populate it as you like.

docs.title: Development (frontend + backend together)
docs.text:
npm run dev

This uses concurrently to launch:

  • Vite frontend at http://localhost:5173 (proxies /api to the backend)
  • Express + MCP backend at http://localhost:3001

The MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint is available at http://localhost:3001/mcp.

docs.title: Verify the setup
docs.text:
# Check Supabase connectivity
curl http://localhost:3001/api/db

# List available Ollama models
curl http://localhost:3001/api/models

docs.title: Claude Desktop (stdio transport)
docs.text:
Edit ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json (macOS) — all paths must be absolute:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cortex": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": [
        "--env-file=/absolute/path/to/cortex/.env",
        "--import=/absolute/path/to/cortex/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.cjs",
        "/absolute/path/to/cortex/src/server/mcp-stdio.ts"
      ]
    }

}

Claude Desktop spawns src/server/mcp-stdio.ts as a subprocess connected via stdio. This file creates a CortexMCPServer via the same createCortexServer() factory used by the HTTP endpoint, so all 12 tools are available identically over both transports.

docs.title: HTTP MCP clients (Cursor, custom agents)
docs.text:
Connect to:

http://localhost:3001/mcp?key=<MCP_ACCESS_KEY>

Or pass the key as a request header:

x-cortex-key: <MCP_ACCESS_KEY>

If MCP_ACCESS_KEY is not set in .env, the auth check is skipped and the endpoint is open.

docs.title: 8. Run the Test Suite

npm test

Tests live in tests/server/ and use vitest with mocked Ollama and Supabase clients. All tests should pass before making any changes to src/server/lib/ or src/server/routes/mcp.ts.

docs.title: Thought Capture
docs.text:
Tools that read from and write to the entries table, filtered to non-wiki sources (web, discord, mcp, api).

Tool Description capture_thought Save a new note or thought; auto-embeds and extracts metadata (topics, type, people, action items) list_thoughts Browse recently captured thoughts in chronological order with optional type/topic/person/days filters search_thoughts Semantic similarity search across captured thoughts only (excludes wiki pages) thought_stats Summary of all captured thoughts: total count, type breakdown, top topics, and top people

docs.title: Wiki Management
docs.text:
Tools that operate on the WikiVault markdown directory (~/Documents/Obsidian/WikiVault/) and keep the Supabase entries table in sync.

Tool Description write_wiki_page Create or overwrite a WikiVault page; auto-generates frontmatter and indexes in Supabase read_wiki_page Read the full content and frontmatter of a WikiVault page by title or file path search_wiki Semantic search across WikiVault pages only, with optional page-type filter list_wiki_pages Browse wiki pages by type/tag via filesystem scan; returns title, type, tags, path (no bodies) append_wiki_log Append a timestamped audit entry to log.md after every significant wiki action

docs.title: Cross-Corpus Search
docs.text: Tool Description search_all Semantic search across all entries — captured thoughts and wiki pages — tagged by source

docs.title: Chat History
docs.text: Tool Description search_messages Semantic search across past AI chat conversation messages in the messages table

docs.title: Migration
docs.text: Tool Description migrate_vault_file One-time import of a MainVault file into WikiVault raw/; strips Dataview blocks, standardises frontmatter, and indexes in Supabase

docs.title: Choosing the right search tool
docs.text: Situation Tool to use User asks about a topic/idea they may have noted before search_thoughts User asks about something that may be in the wiki search_wiki You want the broadest possible context across all data search_all User asks what was discussed in a previous chat session search_messages You know the exact wiki page title read_wiki_page You want to enumerate pages by type (e.g. all people) list_wiki_pages You want recent notes in time order list_thoughts

docs.title: Choosing the right write tool
docs.text: Situation Tool to use Saving an insight, decision, observation, or task capture_thought Creating or updating a structured wiki entry write_wiki_page (always read first — see below) Importing a raw file from MainVault migrate_vault_file Recording that a wiki action was taken append_wiki_log

docs.title: Read-before-write protocol
docs.text:
Never call write_wiki_page without first checking whether the page already exists. Overwriting without reading destroys existing content.

  1. Call read_wiki_page with the page title or path.
  2. If the page exists, merge your changes into the returned body — preserve all sections you are not intentionally replacing.
  3. Call write_wiki_page with the complete merged body.
  4. Call append_wiki_log to record what was changed and why.

If read_wiki_page returns a not-found error, the page does not exist and it is safe to create it with write_wiki_page directly.

docs.title: Search parameter defaults
docs.text:
All search tools share a consistent parameter contract. Values shown are defaults applied when the parameter is omitted.

Parameter Type Default Applies to limit number 10 search_thoughts, search_wiki, search_messages limit number 15 search_all limit number 50 list_wiki_pages threshold number 0.5 search_thoughts, search_wiki threshold number 0.45 search_all (lower for broader recall)

threshold is a cosine similarity score in the range 0–1. Higher values return only closely matching results; lower values cast a wider net. search_messages has no threshold parameter.

docs.title: append_wiki_log
docs.text: Write a one-line timestamped entry to log.md in the WikiVault root. Call this after every write_wiki_page invocation or any other significant wiki decision to maintain a durable audit trail.

docs.title: When to use
docs.text:
• Immediately after write_wiki_page creates or overwrites a page.
  • After any significant decision about WikiVault structure or content (e.g. archiving a page, merging duplicates, deciding not to update a page).
  • Whenever you want a permanent, human-readable record of an action taken in the vault.

append_wiki_log is a pure filesystem append to log.md — it does not call any embedding or database services.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description file_path string ✅ Yes — Relative path of the WikiVault page that was acted on (e.g. wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md) summary string ✅ Yes — One-line description of what was done. Maximum 200 characters.

docs.title: Parameter notes
docs.text:
• file_path — Use a path relative to the WikiVault root, matching the path returned by write_wiki_page or list_wiki_pages. Do not use absolute paths.
  • summary — Keep it concise and action-oriented (e.g. "Created page from captured thoughts about Q2 planning"). The 200-character limit is enforced.

docs.title: Log line format
docs.text:
Each call appends exactly one line to log.md:

ISO-timestamp | tool | file_path | summary

Example:

2026-05-25T04:28:30.000Z | append_wiki_log | wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md | Created page synthesising three captured thoughts about Alice's role in Project Phoenix

The log.md file accumulates entries chronologically and is never truncated by this tool.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A confirmation message indicating the log entry was written, including the timestamp and the path to log.md.

On failure (e.g. WikiVault directory not found, write permission denied), the tool returns an error message with isError: true.

docs.title: After writing a new wiki page
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "write_wiki_page",
  "params": {
    "title": "Alice Smith",
    "type": "wiki_person",
    "body": "## Overview\n\nAlice is the engineering lead for Project Phoenix..."
  }
}

{
  "tool": "append_wiki_log",
  "params": {
    "file_path": "wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md",
    "summary": "Created person page for Alice Smith from three captured thoughts"
  }
}

docs.title: After updating an existing page
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "append_wiki_log",
  "params": {
    "file_path": "wiki/projects/Project-Phoenix.md",
    "summary": "Added Q2 milestone section based on decision captured 2026-05-24"
  }
}

docs.title: After a significant decision (no write)
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "append_wiki_log",
  "params": {
    "file_path": "wiki/concepts/Technical-Debt.md",
    "summary": "Reviewed page — no update needed; content still accurate as of today"
  }
}

docs.title: Recommended workflow
docs.text:
Always pair write_wiki_page with append_wiki_log:

  1. Call read_wiki_page to check whether the page exists.
  2. Call write_wiki_page to create or update the page.
  3. Call append_wiki_log immediately after with the relative file path and a concise summary.

This sequence ensures every write has a corresponding audit entry and the log stays consistent with the vault's actual state.

docs.title: Related tools
docs.text: Tool Relationship write_wiki_page The primary trigger for calling append_wiki_log read_wiki_page Read before writing; then log after writing list_wiki_pages Use to confirm the relative file_path to log

docs.title: capture_thought
docs.text:
Saves a note or thought to Cortex. On every capture the server runs two operations automatically:

  1. Embedding — generates a 4096-dimensional vector (qwen3-embedding via Ollama) and stores it in the entries table with pgvector for semantic retrieval.
  2. Metadata extraction — calls an LLM (via extractMetadata) to classify the thought and pull out structured fields: type, topics, people, and action_items.

Deduplication is handled server-side using a SHA-256 fingerprint of the normalised content. Re-submitting identical content returns duplicate: true and does not create a new row.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Required Default Description content string ✅ Yes — The thought to capture — a clear, self-contained statement

Write content as a single, self-contained statement. Fragmentary phrases yield weaker metadata extraction and lower-quality embeddings.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A text response containing:

Field Description id UUID of the created or existing entry type LLM-assigned content type (e.g. observation, task, idea) topics List of topic tags extracted from the content people People mentioned in the thought action_items Any action items detected duplicate true if identical content was already stored; the existing entry is returned

docs.title: Capturing a decision
docs.text:
{
  "name": "capture_thought",
  "arguments": {
    "content": "Decided to migrate the auth layer to Clerk before the Q3 launch; keeps us off the OAuth maintenance path."
  }
}

docs.title: Capturing a task
docs.text:
{
  "name": "capture_thought",
  "arguments": {
    "content": "Follow up with Jordan about the infrastructure budget by end of week."
  }
}

docs.title: Capturing an observation
docs.text:
{
  "name": "capture_thought",
  "arguments": {
    "content": "Users consistently abandon the onboarding flow at step 4 — the permissions prompt is the likely friction point."
  }
}

docs.title: Deduplication behaviour
docs.text: If you submit the same content a second time, the upsert_entry RPC detects the fingerprint match and returns the existing entry unchanged. The response will include duplicate: true. No new row is written.

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
• Embedding and metadata extraction run in parallel before the database write, so latency scales with the slower of the two (typically the LLM metadata call).
  • The ingestion source is recorded as 'mcp' in the entries table, which allows thought-only search tools to distinguish captured notes from wiki pages.
  • The tool is backed by the shared captureThought() helper in src/server/lib/capture.ts, used by the HTTP REST API, the Discord bot, and this MCP tool — all three paths produce identical entries.

docs.title: Related tools
docs.text:
• search_thoughts — find previously captured thoughts by semantic similarity
  • list_thoughts — browse thoughts chronologically with optional filters
  • thought_stats — aggregate counts, type breakdown, top topics and people

docs.title: list_thoughts
docs.text:
Browse recently captured thoughts in newest-first order. Unlike semantic search tools, list_thoughts issues a direct database query — no embedding is generated — making it the fastest way to retrieve recent entries or enumerate thoughts matching a known attribute.

Use this tool when you want to browse rather than search: recent captures, all tasks, everything tagged with a topic, or everything mentioning a specific person.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
All parameters are optional. Omitting all of them returns the 10 most recently captured thoughts.

Parameter Type Required Default Description limit number No 10 Maximum number of results to return. type string No — Filter by thought type. Must be one of: observation, task, idea, reference, person_note. topic string No — Filter by topic tag (matched against the topics array in the entry's JSONB metadata). person string No — Filter by a person mentioned (matched against the people array in the entry's JSONB metadata). days number No — Restrict results to thoughts captured in the last N days.

docs.title: Filter behaviour
docs.text: All supplied filters are ANDed together. A thought must satisfy every specified filter to appear in results. For example, type=task + person=Alice + days=7 returns only tasks mentioning Alice from the past week.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A formatted text list of matching thoughts, newest first. Each entry includes:

  • Capture date and time
  • Thought type (e.g. task, idea)
  • Topic tags
  • People mentioned
  • Action items (if any)
  • Full thought content

If no thoughts match the filters, the tool returns an empty result with a count of zero.

docs.title: When to use list_thoughts vs. other tools
docs.text: Situation Recommended tool You know the attribute (type, topic, person) list_thoughts You want recent captures without a specific query list_thoughts You have a concept or question to search by meaning search_thoughts You need to search both thoughts and wiki pages search_all You want a count and breakdown of all entries thought_stats

docs.title: Get the 10 most recent thoughts (no filters)
docs.text:
{
  "name": "list_thoughts",
  "arguments": {}
}

docs.title: Show recent tasks from the last 7 days
docs.text:
{
  "name": "list_thoughts",
  "arguments": {
    "type": "task",
    "days": 7
  }
}

docs.title: Show all thoughts mentioning a specific person
docs.text:
{
  "name": "list_thoughts",
  "arguments": {
    "person": "Alice Smith",
    "limit": 25
  }
}

docs.title: Narrow to tasks about a topic from the past month
docs.text:
{
  "name": "list_thoughts",
  "arguments": {
    "type": "task",
    "topic": "machine-learning",
    "days": 30,
    "limit": 20
  }
}

docs.title: Browse all ideas, no time limit
docs.text:
{
  "name": "list_thoughts",
  "arguments": {
    "type": "idea",
    "limit": 50
  }
}

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
list_thoughts queries the entries table in Supabase directly, filtering on source != 'wiki' to exclude WikiVault pages. Type, topic, and person filters use PostgreSQL's JSONB .contains() operator against the metadata column (which is populated at capture time by the LLM metadata-extraction step). The days filter translates to a created_at >= now() - interval 'N days' clause. Results are ordered by created_at descending.

Because no Ollama embedding call is made, this tool completes faster than search_thoughts or search_all and does not require the Ollama service to be running.

docs.title: list_wiki_pages
docs.text:
Browse WikiVault pages with optional filters. Returns title, type, tags, and file path — no body content. Operates entirely from a filesystem scan, so it works even when Supabase is unavailable.

Use list_wiki_pages when you need to enumerate pages ("show me all people", "list every stub") rather than rank by relevance. For relevance-ranked discovery use search_wiki; for full body content use read_wiki_page.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description type string No — Restrict results to one page type (see allowed values below) tag string No — Filter by a single tag (lowercase-kebab) limit number No 50 Maximum number of results to return

docs.title: type allowed values
docs.text: Value Description wiki_person People profiles wiki_project Project pages wiki_concept Concept definitions wiki_area Areas of responsibility or interest wiki_topic Topic overviews raw_article Imported articles raw_book Imported book notes raw_daily Daily notes raw_attachment Attachment files

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A list of page summaries, sorted by title. Each entry includes:

  • title — human-readable page title from frontmatter
  • type — the page type (one of the values above)
  • tags — array of lowercase-kebab topic tags
  • file_path — relative path within the WikiVault directory (e.g. wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md)

Bodies are not returned. Call read_wiki_page with the file_path to retrieve full content.

The following special files are automatically excluded from all results: SCHEMA.md, index.md, log.md.

docs.title: Behavior notes
docs.text:
• No database required. The tool walks the WikiVault directory directly; Supabase does not need to be reachable.
  • Tag filtering matches against the tags array in each page's YAML frontmatter. Pass the tag exactly as it appears in frontmatter (lowercase-kebab format, e.g. machine-learning).
  • Filters combine. Specifying both type and tag returns pages matching both conditions.
  • Limit applies after filtering. Results are capped at limit after type and tag filters are applied.

docs.title: List all people
docs.text:
{
  "name": "list_wiki_pages",
  "arguments": {
    "type": "wiki_person"
  }
}

docs.title: List all stub pages

{

  "arguments": {
    "tag": "stub"
  }

{
  "name": "list_wiki_pages",
  "arguments": {
    "type": "wiki_project",
    "tag": "machine-learning",
    "limit": 20

docs.title: List all pages (no filters, increased limit)

{
  "name": "list_wiki_pages",
  "arguments": {
    "limit": 200

docs.text: Goal Tool Enumerate all pages of a type list_wiki_pages Find pages by meaning / topic search_wiki Read a specific page's content read_wiki_page Search thoughts and wiki together search_all

docs.text:
• search_wiki — semantic search over wiki pages (requires database)
  • read_wiki_page — read full body and frontmatter of a single page
  • write_wiki_page — create or update a wiki page
  • append_wiki_log — add an audit entry after wiki changes

docs.title: migrate_vault_file
docs.text:
One-time import tool that copies a markdown file from MainVault into the WikiVault raw/ hierarchy. During import it:

  • Parses and preserves the original frontmatter (stored as a comment at the bottom of the migrated file)
  • Strips ```dataview ... ``` blocks, replacing them with an HTML comment placeholder
  • Writes standardised frontmatter (type, status, source_path, imported date)
  • Embeds the body and indexes the page in Supabase via upsert_entry
  • Logs the action to the WikiVault audit log
  • Never modifies the original MainVault file

Use this tool during a bulk one-time migration or to import individual articles on demand. To update an already-migrated file you must pass force: true; without it the tool refuses to overwrite.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description source_path string ✅ — Absolute path to the MainVault source file (e.g. /Users/alice/Documents/MainVault/Articles/some-article.md) target_type string (enum) ✅ — Page type that determines which raw/ destination subfolder receives the file. One of: raw_article, raw_book, raw_daily, raw_attachment force boolean ❌ false If true, overwrites the file if it already exists in WikiVault. If false (default) and the file exists, the tool returns an error without writing.

docs.title: target_type values
docs.text:
Value Use for raw_article Articles, essays, web clippings raw_book Book notes and highlights raw_daily Daily notes and journals raw_attachment Other attachments or miscellaneous files

The exact destination subfolder within raw/ is determined by the server's internal mapping for each type.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A text response confirming the import, including the destination path within WikiVault. On failure (e.g. file not found, target exists without force, filesystem error) the response describes the error condition.

docs.title: What happens during import
docs.text:
1. The source file is read from source_path.
  2. Existing frontmatter is parsed via gray-matter.
  3. Dataview code blocks (```dataview ... ```) are stripped and replaced with <!-- dataview block removed -->.
  4. A standardised frontmatter block is written at the top of the new file, incorporating the target_type, a status value (mapped from any existing Status field), the original source_path, and an imported timestamp.
  5. The original frontmatter is appended as a YAML comment at the bottom of the file for reference.
  6. The file is written to the WikiVault raw/ subfolder corresponding to target_type.
  7. The page body is embedded via Ollama and indexed in Supabase (upsert_entry RPC, source='wiki').
  8. The action is logged to the WikiVault audit log.

docs.title: Import a single article
docs.text:
{
  "name": "migrate_vault_file",
  "arguments": {
    "source_path": "/Users/alice/Documents/MainVault/Articles/deep-work-summary.md",
    "target_type": "raw_article"
  }
}

docs.title: Import a book note
docs.text:
{
  "name": "migrate_vault_file",
  "arguments": {
    "source_path": "/Users/alice/Documents/MainVault/Books/atomic-habits.md",
    "target_type": "raw_book"
  }
}

docs.title: Re-import (overwrite) an already-migrated file
docs.text:
{
  "name": "migrate_vault_file",
  "arguments": {
    "source_path": "/Users/alice/Documents/MainVault/Daily/2024-01-15.md",
    "target_type": "raw_daily",
    "force": true
  }
}

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• source_path must be an absolute path. Relative paths are not supported.
  • The original MainVault file is never touched. Only the WikiVault destination is written.
  • force: false (default) is safe. Without force, the tool will not overwrite an existing WikiVault file, making repeated calls to the same source idempotent.
  • Dataview blocks are destructive-stripped. Their query logic is lost; only the placeholder comment remains. Review migrated files if Dataview output was important.
  • Call append_wiki_log manually if you need additional audit entries beyond the automatic one written during import.
  • This tool targets raw/ page types only. To create structured wiki pages (people, projects, concepts, etc.) use write_wiki_page instead.

docs.title: read_wiki_page
docs.text:
Read the full content and frontmatter of a WikiVault page. This is a pure filesystem operation — no database queries or embedding calls are made.

Required before writing. Always call read_wiki_page before write_wiki_page when a page may already exist. write_wiki_page overwrites the file; reading first ensures you preserve existing content and frontmatter fields.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description identifier string Yes — Page title (e.g. "Alice Smith") or relative file path (e.g. "wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md")

docs.title: Identifier resolution
docs.text:
The tool selects its lookup strategy based on the value of identifier:

  • Relative file path — if identifier contains a /, the file is read directly from the WikiVault root. Example: "wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md".
  • Title — if identifier contains no /, the tool scans the WikiVault filesystem via listWikiPages and matches against page titles case-insensitively. Example: "alice smith" will match a page titled "Alice Smith".

Use the file path form when you already know the exact location (faster, unambiguous). Use the title form when you have only the human-readable name.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A formatted text block containing:

  1. All frontmatter fields (title, type, tags, status, created, updated, wikilinks, sources, etc.)
  2. The full markdown body

Returns an error message if no matching page is found.

docs.title: Read by title
docs.text:
{
  "name": "read_wiki_page",
  "arguments": {
    "identifier": "Alice Smith"
  }
}

docs.title: Read by relative file path
docs.text:
{
  "name": "read_wiki_page",
  "arguments": {
    "identifier": "wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md"
  }
}

docs.title: Case-insensitive title lookup
docs.text:
{
  "name": "read_wiki_page",
  "arguments": {
    "identifier": "machine learning"
  }
}

This will match a page titled "Machine Learning", "machine learning", or any other capitalisation variant.

docs.title: Read-before-write pattern
docs.text:
The canonical update workflow:

  1. Call read_wiki_page with the page title or path.
  2. Inspect the returned frontmatter and body.
  3. Merge your changes into the existing content.
  4. Call write_wiki_page with the complete updated body and all preserved fields.
  5. Call append_wiki_log to record the action.

Skipping step 1 risks clobbering existing data — frontmatter fields like created, wikilinks, cortex_ids, and page_sources are not automatically carried forward by write_wiki_page unless you supply them explicitly.

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
• Implemented in src/server/routes/mcp.ts; filesystem operations are handled by src/server/lib/wiki.ts (readWikiPage, listWikiPages).
  • Title lookup iterates the result of listWikiPages (a directory scan) and compares titles case-insensitively. Only the frontmatter title field is matched — not filenames.
  • No Supabase or Ollama calls are made; the tool works even if the database or inference service is unavailable.
  • The WikiVault root is configured via the WIKI_VAULT_PATH environment variable (default: ~/Documents/Obsidian/WikiVault/).

docs.title: search_all
docs.text:
Perform a single semantic search across all entries in Cortex: captured thoughts (from web, Discord, MCP, and API sources) and WikiVault pages together. Results are ranked by relevance and labelled by source so you can tell at a glance whether a hit came from a thought or a wiki page.

Use search_all when you are unsure whether the information you are looking for was saved as a quick note or as a structured wiki entry. For narrower queries, prefer search_thoughts or search_wiki.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description query string yes — The search query. Embedded with qwen3-embedding and compared against all entries using cosine similarity. limit number no 15 Maximum number of results to return. threshold number no 0.45 Minimum cosine similarity score (0–1). Lower than other search tools to maximise recall across both corpora.

docs.title: Threshold note
docs.text: The default threshold of 0.45 is intentionally more permissive than search_thoughts (0.5) and search_wiki (0.5). This trades precision for recall, surfacing relevant entries that might otherwise be missed when you are exploring unfamiliar territory. Raise it toward 0.6–0.7 if you are getting too many loosely-related results.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A text response listing matched entries in ranked order. Each entry includes:

  • Source label — [thought] with a subtype (e.g. idea, task) or [wiki:page_type] (e.g. [wiki:wiki_person], [wiki:wiki_concept])
  • Title or date — wiki page title, or capture timestamp for thoughts
  • Tags — topic tags attached to the entry
  • Excerpt — up to 300 characters of the entry body
  • Similarity score — the cosine similarity value

Returns an empty result set (not an error) when no entries exceed the threshold.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: search_all embeds query using Ollama (qwen3-embedding, 4096-d vectors) and calls the Supabase match_entries RPC with source_filter: null and no page-type filter. This scans the unified entries table across all source values — thoughts captured from any ingestion path and wiki pages indexed with source='wiki'. Results are sorted by cosine distance and truncated to limit.

docs.title: Broadest possible recall
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_all",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "machine learning model deployment"
  }
}

Returns up to 15 results from both thoughts and wiki pages, labelled by source.

docs.title: Increase result count and tighten threshold
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_all",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "Alice's feedback on the Q3 roadmap",
    "limit": 25,
    "threshold": 0.55
  }
}

Returns up to 25 results with a higher similarity bar, filtering out loosely-related entries.

docs.title: Exploring an unfamiliar topic
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_all",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "distributed tracing observability",
    "limit": 20,
    "threshold": 0.4
  }
}

Drops the threshold below the default to surface even loosely-related notes and wiki pages when you are not sure how the topic was originally framed.

docs.title: When to use search_all vs. other search tools
docs.text: Situation Recommended tool Not sure if info is in a thought or wiki page search_all Definitely looking in captured notes only search_thoughts Definitely looking in wiki pages only search_wiki Looking in past AI chat conversations search_messages Know the exact wiki page title read_wiki_page Want to browse by type chronologically list_thoughts or list_wiki_pages

docs.title: search_messages
docs.text:
Search across all past AI chat conversation messages by semantic similarity. Use this tool when you need to recall something discussed in a previous chat session, not something explicitly captured as a thought or written into a wiki page.

search_messages queries the messages table — the log of user and assistant turns from the streaming chat endpoint — rather than the entries table that backs search_thoughts and search_wiki. If the information you are looking for was part of a conversation (not deliberately saved), this is the right tool.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description query string Yes — What to search for in chat history limit number No 10 Maximum number of results to return

docs.title: Parameter notes
docs.text:
• query — a natural-language phrase or question. The query is embedded and matched against stored message embeddings via cosine similarity.
  • limit — controls how many matching messages are returned. Raise this if you need broader coverage of a conversation thread; lower it to keep responses concise.

There is no threshold parameter for this tool. Similarity filtering is handled internally by the Supabase search_messages RPC.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A formatted text block containing the top-N matching messages, each showing:

  • Role — user or assistant
  • Content — the full message text
  • Timestamp — when the message was recorded

Results are ranked by semantic similarity to the query, most relevant first.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Cortex embeds the query string using the configured Ollama embedding model.
  2. The embedding is passed to the Supabase search_messages RPC, which runs a vector similarity search against the messages table.
  3. The RPC returns the closest matches ranked by cosine distance.
  4. Results are formatted and returned as a text response.

The messages table is populated automatically by the streaming chat endpoint each time a user sends a message or the assistant replies. No manual capture step is required.

docs.title: When to use this tool vs. others
docs.text: Situation Tool Looking for something discussed in a past chat session search_messages Looking for a thought explicitly saved with capture_thought search_thoughts Looking for content in a wiki page search_wiki Searching across everything (thoughts + wiki) search_all

docs.title: Basic search
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "search_messages",
  "params": {
    "query": "what did we decide about the project timeline?"
  }
}

docs.title: Search with a higher result limit
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "search_messages",
  "params": {
    "query": "machine learning model recommendations",
    "limit": 25
  }
}

docs.title: Recalling a specific discussion
docs.text:
{
  "tool": "search_messages",
  "params": {
    "query": "Alice's feedback on the onboarding flow",
    "limit": 5
  }
}

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only covers messages from the Cortex chat interface. Thoughts captured via the web UI, Discord, or direct capture_thought calls are not in this table — use search_thoughts for those.
  • There is no date or role filter; all matching messages regardless of speaker or session are returned together.
  • If a topic was discussed briefly and the message did not produce a strong embedding match, it may not appear in results. Consider broadening the query or increasing limit.

docs.title: search_thoughts
docs.text:
Search captured thoughts by meaning using semantic similarity. Unlike keyword search, this tool finds notes that are conceptually related to your query even when the exact words differ.

Scope: thoughts only (sources: web, discord, mcp, api). Wiki pages are excluded. Use search_all for combined results across both thoughts and wiki, or search_wiki for wiki pages only.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description query string Yes — What to search for limit number No 10 Maximum number of results to return threshold number No 0.5 Minimum similarity score (0–1); results below this are excluded

docs.title: Threshold guidance
docs.text:
Goal Suggested threshold High precision, exact topic 0.7 – 0.8 Balanced (default) 0.5 Broad recall, uncertain phrasing 0.3 – 0.4

Lower the threshold when you are unsure how a thought was originally phrased or when the concept may have been captured tangentially. Raise it to filter out loosely related results.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The query string is embedded using the configured Ollama embedding model. The resulting vector is compared against stored thought embeddings using cosine similarity via the Supabase match_entries RPC, filtered to non-wiki sources. Only results meeting or exceeding threshold are returned, ranked from most to least similar, up to limit results.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A ranked list of matching thoughts. Each result includes:

  • Date — when the thought was captured
  • Type — the classified thought type (e.g. observation, task, idea)
  • Topics — extracted topic tags
  • People — mentioned individuals
  • Action items — any action items extracted from the thought
  • Content — the full text of the thought

Returns an empty list when no results meet the threshold. Does not return thoughts from wiki pages regardless of threshold.

docs.title: Basic search
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_thoughts",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "product roadmap priorities for Q3"
  }
}

docs.title: High-precision search with fewer results
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_thoughts",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "decision to migrate to microservices",
    "limit": 5,
    "threshold": 0.72
  }
}

docs.title: Broad recall when phrasing is uncertain
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_thoughts",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "meeting with Alice about the budget",
    "limit": 20,
    "threshold": 0.35
  }
}

docs.title: When to use this tool
docs.text:
• The user asks what they previously noted about a topic, person, or event.
  • You want to surface relevant context before responding to a question.
  • You need to check whether a thought already exists before capturing a duplicate.

Prefer search_all when you do not know whether the relevant content was captured as a thought or written as a wiki page.

Prefer list_thoughts when you want chronological browsing with structured filters (type, topic, person, date range) rather than semantic ranking.

docs.title: search_wiki
docs.text:
Search WikiVault pages by semantic similarity. Results are ranked by relevance and include a similarity score, page type, title, tags, and a 200-character body excerpt.

Use this tool when you believe content exists in the wiki but don't know the exact page title. To browse pages by type without a query, use list_wiki_pages. To search across both wiki pages and captured thoughts together, use search_all.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description query string Yes — What to search for limit number No 10 Maximum number of results to return threshold number No 0.5 Minimum similarity score (0–1); results below this score are excluded type string No — Restrict results to one page type (see enum below)

docs.title: type enum values
docs.text: Value Description wiki_person People pages wiki_project Project pages wiki_concept Concept pages wiki_area Area pages wiki_topic Topic pages raw_article Imported articles raw_book Imported books raw_daily Daily notes raw_attachment Attachments

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A ranked list of matching wiki pages. Each result includes:

  • Similarity score — cosine similarity between the query and the page embedding
  • Page type — one of the type enum values above
  • Title — the page's human-readable title
  • Tags — topic tags attached to the page
  • Body excerpt — up to 200 characters of the page body

Pages are ordered from most to least similar. Results below the threshold are excluded.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The query string is embedded using Ollama's configured embedding model.
  2. The resulting vector is compared against all wiki page embeddings stored in the Supabase entries table (rows with source='wiki') using the match_entries RPC and cosine similarity.
  3. If a type parameter is provided, it is passed as a page_type filter to the RPC, restricting matches to that page type.
  4. Results meeting the similarity threshold are returned, ranked by score, up to limit entries.

docs.title: Basic semantic search
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_wiki",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "machine learning approaches for recommendation systems"
  }
}

docs.title: Search restricted to a page type
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_wiki",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "Alice Smith",
    "type": "wiki_person"
  }
}

docs.title: Narrow search with a higher threshold
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_wiki",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "GraphQL schema design patterns",
    "limit": 5,
    "threshold": 0.75,
    "type": "wiki_concept"
  }
}

docs.title: Broad search with more results
docs.text:
{
  "name": "search_wiki",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "Q3 product roadmap",
    "limit": 20,
    "threshold": 0.4
  }
}

docs.title: Choosing the right search tool
docs.text: Situation Tool You know the exact page title or file path read_wiki_page You want to browse all pages of a given type list_wiki_pages You want wiki pages only, searching by meaning search_wiki ← you are here You want captured thoughts only, searching by meaning search_thoughts You want the broadest search across all content search_all

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• search_wiki only searches pages with source='wiki' in the entries table. Captured thoughts (from web, Discord, MCP, or API) are excluded.
  • Lowering threshold (e.g. to 0.3) increases recall but may return loosely related pages. Raising it (e.g. to 0.7) returns only close matches.
  • Pages must be indexed in Supabase to appear in results. Pages written via write_wiki_page are indexed automatically. If a page was added directly to the filesystem, run a reindex operation before searching.
  • The type filter is applied at the database level, not post-hoc — combining it with a high limit will not waste result slots on other page types.

docs.title: thought_stats
docs.text:
Get an aggregate summary of everything captured in Cortex. Returns total thought count, a breakdown by type, the ten most frequently occurring topics, and the ten most frequently mentioned people — all computed in a single pass over the entries table with no embedding or LLM inference required.

Use this tool to: - Quickly gauge how populated the knowledge base is - Surface dominant themes and recurring contacts - Verify that new captures are being classified correctly - Orient yourself before a deeper search or analysis session

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
This tool takes no parameters.

Parameter Type Required Default Description (none) — — — Stats are always computed across the full corpus of non-wiki entries.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A formatted text block containing:

Field Description total Total number of captured thoughts (non-wiki entries) by_type Count for each thought type: observation, task, idea, reference, person_note top_topics Top 10 topic tags ranked by frequency of occurrence across all thoughts top_people Top 10 people mentioned, ranked by frequency

Results are computed in-memory from the JSONB metadata column of the entries table. Only entries with source != 'wiki' are included — wiki pages are excluded from all stats.

}

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
• No inference required. thought_stats queries only the entries table — no Ollama embedding call or LLM metadata extraction is made. It is the fastest MCP tool to call.
  • In-memory aggregation. All non-wiki rows are fetched with an exact count, then iterated once in the server process to tally type distribution and topic/people frequency from the metadata JSONB column.
  • Scope is fixed. There is no way to filter by date range or source — the tool always reports on the entire corpus. To examine a slice of thoughts, use list_thoughts with its days, type, or topic filters instead.
  • Reflects current state. Because stats are computed fresh on each call against the live entries table, the numbers always reflect the current state of the database.

docs.title: write_wiki_page
docs.text:
Creates or overwrites a WikiVault page. Used to maintain LLM-curated wiki entries for people, projects, concepts, areas, topics, and raw imported content.

⚠ Read before you write. Always call read_wiki_page first if the page may already exist. This tool performs a full overwrite — calling it without reading first will silently discard existing content.

docs.title: What happens on write
docs.text:
1. A kebab-case file path is derived from title and type (e.g. wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md).
  2. writeWikiPage merges the call with any existing frontmatter: created is preserved, updated is bumped to now, and [[wikilinks]] in the body are automatically extracted and stored in the frontmatter wikilinks[] array.
  3. The page is written to the WikiVault filesystem with auto-generated YAML frontmatter. Do not include frontmatter in body.
  4. The body is embedded via Ollama (qwen3-embedding) and upserted into Supabase via the upsert_entry RPC (source='wiki').
  5. For new pages, index.md is rebuilt. Every write should be followed by append_wiki_log to maintain the audit trail.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description title string ✅ — Human-readable page title, e.g. "Alice Smith". Used to derive the file name. type string (enum) ✅ — Page type — determines the destination subfolder. See Page types below. body string ✅ — Full markdown body. Do not include YAML frontmatter — it is generated automatically. tags string[] ❌ [] Topic tags in lowercase-kebab format, e.g. ["machine-learning", "nlp"]. page_sources string[] ❌ [] Source URLs, raw/ file paths, or entry UUIDs that this page was derived from. cortex_ids string[] ❌ [] UUIDs from the Supabase entries table that this wiki page synthesises. Enables traceability back to captured thoughts. status string (enum) ❌ "active" Page lifecycle status: active, archived, or stub.

docs.title: Page types
docs.text: Value Destination subfolder Typical use wiki_person wiki/people/ Person profiles wiki_project wiki/projects/ Project pages wiki_concept wiki/concepts/ Definitions, ideas wiki_area wiki/areas/ Life/work areas wiki_topic wiki/topics/ Topic overviews raw_article raw/articles/ Imported articles raw_book raw/books/ Imported book notes raw_daily raw/daily/ Daily notes raw_attachment raw/attachments/ Misc imported files

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A text response confirming: - The file path the page was written to - Whether it was created new or updated - The number of wikilinks extracted from the body - Confirmation of Supabase indexing

On error, isError: true is set and the text describes the failure (e.g. invalid type, filesystem write error, embedding failure).

docs.title: Create a new person page
docs.text:
{
  "name": "write_wiki_page",
  "arguments": {
    "title": "Alice Smith",
    "type": "wiki_person",
    "body": "## Overview\n\nAlice is an ML researcher at DeepMind focused on [[Reinforcement Learning]].\n\n## Notes\n\n- Met at NeurIPS 2024\n- Working on reward modelling for [[RLHF]]",
    "tags": ["ml", "reinforcement-learning", "deepmind"],
    "status": "active"
  }
}

docs.title: Update an existing page (read-first pattern)
docs.text:
// Step 1 — always read first
{
  "name": "read_wiki_page",
  "arguments": {
    "identifier": "Alice Smith"
  }
}

// Step 2 — write with updated content
{
  "name": "write_wiki_page",
  "arguments": {
    "title": "Alice Smith",
    "type": "wiki_person",
    "body": "## Overview\n\nAlice is an ML researcher at DeepMind focused on [[Reinforcement Learning]].\n\n## Notes\n\n- Met at NeurIPS 2024\n- Working on reward modelling for [[RLHF]]\n- Joined as advisor on [[Project Athena]] in Jan 2025",
    "tags": ["ml", "reinforcement-learning", "deepmind"],
    "status": "active"
  }
}

// Step 3 — log the action
{
  "name": "append_wiki_log",
  "arguments": {
    "file_path": "wiki/people/Alice-Smith.md",
    "summary": "Added Project Athena advisor note"
  }
}

docs.title: Create a project stub with source tracing
docs.text:
{
  "name": "write_wiki_page",
  "arguments": {
    "title": "Project Athena",
    "type": "wiki_project",
    "body": "## Status\n\nEarly-stage. See [[Alice Smith]] for context.\n\n## Goals\n\nTBD.",
    "tags": ["active-project"],
    "cortex_ids": ["3f2a1b4c-8d9e-4f1a-b2c3-d4e5f6a7b8c9"],
    "status": "stub"
  }
}

docs.title: Wikilinks
docs.text: Any [[Page Title]] reference in body is automatically extracted and written to the frontmatter wikilinks array. This enables forward-link tracking across the vault. You do not need to declare wikilinks separately — just write them naturally in the body.

docs.title: Frontmatter generated automatically
docs.text:
The tool builds YAML frontmatter from your parameters plus system fields. Example output for a person page:

---
title: Alice Smith
type: wiki_person
status: active
tags:
  - ml
  - reinforcement-learning
  - deepmind
wikilinks:
  - Reinforcement Learning
  - RLHF
page_sources: []
cortex_ids: []
created: 2025-01-15T10:23:00.000Z
updated: 2025-04-02T14:05:00.000Z
---

Never include a frontmatter block in your body argument. If you do, it will appear as literal text in the rendered page.
